一、渭水有月
老君驾鹤离去时，满天霞光正盛。
水镜站在新冢前，看着那方她用了一千三百年才等来的人。
破军没有动。
他像一尊石像，立在原地，银灰色的眼眸里翻涌着三千年修为都压不住的惊涛。他想上前，又怕上前——怕这又是一场梦，怕伸手的瞬间，她便会像之前无数次梦里那样，化作烟云散去。
水镜却笑了。
那笑容与千年前一模一样——唇角先扬，眼底后暖，像春日的渭水，冰层下终于涌出活水。
“萧将军，”她轻声说，“你还要我等多久？”
破军的喉结滚动了一下。
他向前迈出一步，两步，三步——最后几乎是踉跄着奔到她面前。
这一次，他伸手触到的，不再是冰冷的残魂，不是水底的幻影，不是梦里一触即碎的泡影。
是温热的、真实的、有呼吸的——
她。
水镜微微仰头，望着他。一千三百年了，他的眉眼还是那个样子，只是鬓边多了几缕白发，眼底多了几分她不忍细看的疲惫。
“破军。”她轻声唤他“你老了。”
破军的声音哑得几乎听不清：
“等得太久了。”
水镜眼眶微红，却仍是笑着。

她抬手，指尖轻轻抚过他鬓边的白发，抚过他眉间那道因千年寻觅而刻下的细纹，抚过他唇角那道终于不再是紧抿的弧度。
“以后，”她说，“不用等了。”
破军握住她的手。
那双手也曾握过剑，握过千军万马的帅印，握过无数个孤寂长夜里自己给自己温的酒。此刻却只是轻轻握着她的指尖，像握着一件失而复得的、世间最珍贵的易碎品。
“水镜。”他唤她。
“嗯。”
“水镜。”
“在。”
“水镜——”
“破军，”她打断他，眼底有泪光，却仍是笑着，“我在。一直都在。”
远处，渭水岸边，联盟众人静静望着这一幕。
永珍靠在杨思纯肩上，泪流满面。她额间那滴泪痕状的淡银色印记，此刻正微微发烫，像母亲隔着时空轻轻抚过她的脸。
杨思纯揽着她的肩，没有说话。他只是望着那两道终于并肩而立的身影，眉心的鲤印在暮色中柔柔发光。
惜若抱着剑，眼眶微红，嘴上却不饶人：“哼，三千年功力，就这点出息。手抖成那样，还化神巅峰呢。”
江流云轻咳一声，示意她少说两句。
胡嗖——依然困在小靖躯体里的胡嗖——捋了捋并不存在的长须，悠悠道：“三千年，换一个圆满。值。”
小靖——困在胡嗖躯体里的小靖——难得没有反驳，只是轻轻点头。
柳如是哭得稀里哗啦，一边抹泪一边往嘴里塞桂花糕，含糊不清地说：“太感人了呜呜呜……我要把这一幕画下来……呜呜呜……”
沈轻烟递给她一方帕子，唇角却也不自觉地上扬。
唯有白虹站在人群最边缘。

她望着渭水边那两道身影，望着破军终于不再孤寂的背影，望着水镜眼中那千年未变的温柔。
她忽然想起那夜在书房里，胡嗖对她说的话：
“喜欢一个人没有错。克制不是压抑，是珍惜——珍惜他，珍惜他选择的人，也珍惜你自己。”
她望着水镜。
那是一个等了一千三百年、却从未怨恨过的女子。是一个以身祭水、护佑苍生、却从未后悔过的神祇。是一个终于等到了圆满、却仍笑得那样温柔、那样干净的魂魄。

1. There is a moon on the Wei River
When Laojun left on the crane, the sky was full of glow.
Shui Jing stood in front of the new tomb, looking at the person she had waited for for thirteen hundred years.
Po Jun didn't move.
He stood like a stone statue, his silver-grey eyes filled with waves that even three thousand years of cultivation could not suppress. He wanted to step forward, but was afraid to step forward - afraid that this would be another dream, afraid that the moment he reached out, she would turn into smoke and disperse like in countless previous dreams.
Shui Jing smiled.
The smile is exactly the same as it was a thousand years ago - the corners of the lips are raised first, and the eyes are warm, like the Wei River in spring, when living water finally gushes out from under the ice.
"General Xiao," she said softly, "how long do you want me to wait?"
Po Jun's Adam's apple rolled.
He took one step forward, two steps, three steps - finally almost staggering towards her.
This time, what he reached out to touch was no longer the cold remnant soul, nor the phantom under the water, nor the bubbles that shattered at the touch of a dream.
It's warm, real, breathing -
her.
Shui Jing raised his head slightly and looked at him. Thirteen hundred years later, his features were still the same, but there were a few strands of white hair on his temples, and there was a bit more tiredness in his eyes that she couldn't bear to look at.
"Pojun." She called him softly, "You are old."
Po Jun's voice was so mute that it was almost inaudible:
"It's been too long to wait."
Shui Jing's eyes were slightly red, but she was still smiling.
She raised her hand and gently stroked the white hair on his temples with her fingertips, stroked the fine lines between his eyebrows that had been carved for a thousand years of searching, and stroked the curve of the corner of his lips that was no longer tight.
"In the future," she said, "there's no need to wait."
Po Jun held her hand.
Those hands have also held swords, held the seal of command of thousands of troops, and held the wine that he warmed for himself in countless long lonely nights. At this moment, he was just holding her fingertips gently, as if he was holding a lost and found, the most precious and fragile object in the world.
"Shui Jing." He called her.
"Yeah."
"Water mirror."
"Here."
"Shui Jing——"
"Pojun," she interrupted him, with tears in her eyes but still smiling, "I'm here. I've always been here."
In the distance, on the shore of the Wei River, everyone in the alliance watched this scene quietly.
Yongzhen leaned on Yang Sichun's shoulder, tears streaming down her face. The tear-shaped pale silver mark on her forehead was slightly hot at the moment, like a mother gently caressing her face across time and space.
Yang Sichun held her shoulders and said nothing. He just looked at the two figures who finally stood side by side, the carp marks between their eyebrows glowing softly in the dusk.
Xiruo hugged the sword, her eyes were slightly red, but her mouth was unforgiving: "Huh, three thousand years of skill, this is all. With your hands shaking like that, you are still at the peak of divine transformation."
Jiang Liuyun coughed lightly and motioned for her to say less.
Hu Sou - Hu Sou who was still trapped in Xiao Jing's body - stroked his non-existent long beard and said leisurely: "Three thousand years to change to perfection. It's worth it."
Xiao Jing—Xiao Jing trapped in Hu Sou’s body—rarely did not refute, and just nodded lightly.
Liu Rushi burst into tears, wiping her tears while stuffing sweet-scented osmanthus cake into her mouth, and said vaguely: "It's so touching... I want to draw this scene... Wuwu..."
Shen Qingyan handed her a handkerchief, but the corners of her lips rose unconsciously.
Only Bai Hong stood at the edge of the crowd.
She looked at the two figures by the Wei River, at Po Jun's back who was finally no longer lonely, and at the tenderness in Shui Jing's eyes that had not changed for thousands of years.
She suddenly remembered what Hu Sou said to her that night in the study:
"There is nothing wrong with liking someone. Restraint is not suppression, it is cherishing - cherishing him, cherishing the person he chooses, and cherishing yourself."
She looked into the water mirror.
That is a woman who has waited for thirteen hundred years but has never resented her. He is a god who sacrificed his body to water to protect the common people, but never regretted it. It is a soul that has finally waited for perfection, but still smiles so gently and so cleanly.
